results.output: For your use case, the local box is fast for everyday drafting, but it is not as polished as the best cloud assistant. The faster local model produced 92.28 tokens/sec, which means it can return a usable draft quickly enough for a partner to read and edit. The slower model produced 10.89 tokens/sec, which is slow for repeated questions. Transcription ran at 28x real time, so a recording can be turned into text much faster than listening to it. On quality, the best local models scored 3.00 out of 5 for send readiness, meaning a professional would usually need light edits before filing or sending. The best cloud assistant scored 4.37 out of 5, meaning it is often close to ready with only small checks. The local model scored 93% on summarisation accuracy traps, so it is reliable for pulling out the main points, but it can still miss nuance. It chose and called the correct tool in 91% of tasks, with zero malformed calls, meaning no broken instructions. However, it serves one user at full speed at a time, and work for clients still needs human review because it may state a detail the source does not support.
